name: Henky

attributes.attribute: Scottish folkloric figure, a common name for a fairy person in Orkney and the Shetlands
fairy people could be detected because they limped, or henked, when they danced
folklore does not explain the reason for the fairy limp

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Henky is a Scottish folkloric figure. In the islands off Scotland, Orkney and the Shetlands, fairy people could be detected by their limp. They limped, or henked, when they danced. Folklore does not explain the reason for this handicap. Henky thus became a common name for a fairy person in that region.
objective: Document Henky, the limping fairy of the Scottish islands.
key_results: Record the name as a common term for a fairy person.
Describe the limp, or henking, that revealed fairies.
Note that folklore gives no reason for the handicap.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): Henky entry.
